title: Fast O(n) Common-ID Finder Using set
prompt: Write find_common(list_a, list_b) that returns a sorted list of IDs present in both lists using set intersection (avoiding O(n^2) nested loops).
hints: Convert both lists to sets and use & (intersection).
solution:
def find_common(list_a, list_b):
    return sorted(set(list_a) & set(list_b))
explanation: Set intersection runs in O(len(a) + len(b)) average time instead of O(len(a) * len(b)).

title: Complexity & Data Structure Choice
prompt: Choose the fastest approach for membership checks.
hints: Hash tables give O(1) average lookup.
explanation: set and dict use hash tables for O(1) average-case membership testing.

questions.question: You need to check 100,000 times whether an ID exists in a collection of 50,000 valid IDs. Which collection gives O(1) average lookup?
questions.explanation: set (and dict keys) use hash tables for O(1) average-case lookup, whereas list and tuple scan linearly in O(n).

title: set vs list membership
front: What is the average time complexity of `x in c` for a `set` vs a `list`?
back: `set`: O(1) average time (hash lookup). `list`: O(n) linear scan.
